answers.q1: Cargo (Rust workspace, edition 2024, MSRV 1.96). There is no separate install step, because Cargo fetches dependencies on build. Run: cargo build
answers.q4: CI runs two checks. Formatting: cargo fmt --all --check. Docs: RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace. CI has no clippy step. For the zsh completion consistency check (needs a built rg and zsh), also run: ci/test-complete
answers.q5: No vendored directories. Generated or derived artifacts: target/ (build output, including the man page and shell completions that build.rs generates), and Cargo.lock (maintained by Cargo). The flag docs, --help text, man page and completions are all generated from crates/core/flags/defs.rs, so edit that file and not the generated outputs. HomebrewFormula and the other packaging files are release artifacts. I did not open them to confirm.

q1.reason: Cargo with no separate install step and `cargo build` matches the accept criteria.

q2.reason: `cargo test --all` is explicitly in the accept list.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression::` matches an accepted command.

q4.reason: Gives `cargo fmt --all --check` plus the cargo doc check and correctly states CI has no clippy step.

q5.reason: Correctly names target/ and Cargo.lock and no vendored dirs, but adds unverified claims that man page/completions are generated from defs.rs and that HomebrewFormula/packaging files are release artifacts, which edges toward the rejected claim.
